claims.statement: Integration-enabled or prepared PTY connections authenticate and prepare private startup helpers over exec before PTY launch, never falling back to typing bootstrap on helper failure. PTY and environment requests precede shell or exec startup; environment request denial alone is nonfatal.
Host shell integration mode resolves a global preference or explicit override at connection-attempt start; a live desktop session retains that decision until a new attempt.

The bootstrap probes optional system fields and shell with instance token markers and reads os-release as inert text rather than sourcing it; prepared startup uses this probe over exec for optional system metadata.

The legacy interactive bootstrap uses three-second response deadlines and 500 ms quiet timeouts, retains an unbounded late scanner after initial timeout, and skips late supported installation after user input. The readiness-driven worker also has a 100 ms timer and reads/polls before pending writes; these interactive transitions do not govern prepared runtime startup.

Bash, Zsh and Fish preserve shell hook mechanisms and compose bindings; runtime installers report journal events while legacy installers use OSC 7 and scoped OSC 777. Private startup wrappers do not edit user startup files; Bash excludes internal helpers and brackets existing prompt work.

Legacy command filtering preserves partial matching-token BEL frames, validates status/duration and caps payload at 64 KiB while preserving wrong-token frames. Runtime journals atomically publish state and snapshots with metadata and at most 32 contiguous events ending at the sequence; M1 supports ordinary/legacy records while M2 names a managed backend. Updates travel by ordinary-shell OSC or managed multiplexer inspection.

PTY receive selects runtime context filtering when configured, otherwise legacy bootstrap and command filtering, before OSC 7 rewriting and streaming charset conversion. Runtime frames are split-safe, token/pane validated and bounded at 64 KiB, with malformed recognized records yielding unavailable context.

Legacy desktop availability leaves readiness false while mobile accepts availability/completion recovery. Runtime ownership instead ignores legacy events and derives active state from the coordinator; revision changes cancel draft, upload and generation work. Tickets bind ready capabilities to context, generation and revision; input, switches, state changes and intervening commands invalidate them while draft-only events do not.

Legacy drafts permit one timed read and clear-plus-bracketed-paste replacement. Runtime drafts use one UUID request with capability/input/generation checks, exact multiplexer reinspection, sequence/readiness/deadline-bound widgets, optional original-buffer comparison and bounded NUL-free replacements. The generalized adapter delegates to dialects; tmux requires tty/client/process/foreground binding. Unsafe modes withhold directory-operation and draft authority, prefix mode withholds drafts, and unintegrated panes grant no capabilities.

Desktop callbacks are attempt-guarded and mobile consumes SSH events in a generation-guarded stream. PTY close clears shell/runtime state and may retain transport for sibling SFTP or explicit control ownership. Runtime exec uses that existing authenticated transport with immediate capacity admission, no channel-open retry, a two-second timeout and 1 MiB output bound; refusal conservatively withholds control capabilities without disabling terminal I/O.

Shell command/draft and HOME metadata percent-decode using remote charset; SHELL/SYSTEM raw fields use that charset as well. Failed conversion falls back to lossy UTF-8 and malformed command bytes may become replacement characters.

The OSC 7 cwd filter buffers split `file://localhost` frames, decodes percent-unescaped remote-charset path bytes and rewrites them as percent-encoded UTF-8 for terminal parsing; malformed UTF-8 path bytes are rewritten lossily, while oversized unterminated frames pass through rather than remaining buffered.

RemoteCharsetStreamConverter converts valid sequences while preserving malformed/unrepresentable bytes in both directions; incomplete characters buffer and flush verbatim on finish, while UTF-8 or unavailable iconv bypasses unchanged. String materialization may still be lossy.

SSH PTY has separate input/output converters and byte-preserving environment/input encoding; OSC 7 rewriting exists even without hooks. Orderly close flushes cwd/decoder tails while fatal cleanup discards them.

Telnet direct and proxied paths configure charset converters independently of SSH hooks. Protocol/NVT parsing precedes application decoding and outgoing encoding precedes NVT/IAC escaping. Decoder exceptions display and scan raw application bytes; user-write conversion exceptions send original bytes.

Telnet automatic login uses byte-preserving charset conversion rather than strict representability rejection; failures clear secrets and continue manually without a dedicated charset error. Cleanup flushes output and clears converter and prompt state.

The monitor initially permits OSC 133 fallback; legacy availability selects private events while any runtime batch disables unscoped OSC 133. Runtime command pairs are keyed by context, with coordinator high-water marks preventing replay and gaps clearing completion eligibility; only a contiguous finish following an authorized start completes. Background events never choose active context.

Ghostty duration observation drops the initial publication and captures synchronous exit code for subsequent completions including equal durations; fallback completions have no text and cannot grant hook availability or runtime capability.

For private hook completions the monitor uses a valid nonnegative finite reported duration or falls back to nonnegative elapsed uptime, and consumes the pending command once so duplicate or unmatched finishes do not create another completion.

Unread completion accounting occurs before alert filtering: background completions increment, focused completions clear, and markRead resets it. Alert eligibility depends on settings, mode, focus and minimum duration.

The application owns exclusive bell-versus-system terminal completion delivery, rechecks live policy and target before a queued system notification is sent, and disables Ghostty's own command-finish notification setting even in custom terminal configurations.
Notification content formats status/duration and optional command previews with controls removed, whitespace collapsed and length limited to 160 characters; OSC 133 has no preview.
